newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries firmer in London, focus on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries firmer in London, focus on Wall Street.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were slightly better bid in London on Monday with the market looking to the Wall Street opening for direction, analysts said.

A dearth of economic data and widespread expectations Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting will be a non-event, have left Treasuries to focus on their safe haven status from the U.S. stock market plunge last Friday.
"In terms of domestic factors it's hard to think of much moving the market this week," said Dick Howard, senior economist at Julius Baer Investments in London.
"The equity market is the thing to watch -- if Wall Street continues to be weak then bonds will benefit."
Treasuries got a boost late on Friday in New York and in Tokyo trade on Monday after the Dow Jones index closed 247 points lower, its biggest point drop since the 1987 stock market crash.
Howard said the traditional safe haven was the shortest, highest quality paper available. "But people are pretty relaxed across the (Treasury) curve so the whole of it could benefit."
By 0945 GMT, 30-year T-bonds were at 97-28 to yield 6.54 percent, up from 97-24 in Tokyo and New York. Ten-year paper was at 99-09 up from 99-06 in Tokyo and 99-05 in New York.
The dollar had recovered from its early dip against the mark by mid-morning to stand at 1.8117/22, but traders said it was struggling to hold 1.81.
One dealer said the market had fully priced in no rate move at Tuesday's FOMC, leaving it with little to do in the run up to the meeting.
"I wouldn't have thought the market will do anything before the meeting, not now," he said.

He predicted a wary opening for the Dow on Monday. "The sell-off was so late on Friday. There might be some profit taking for those who did manage to get short, so we might see the market rally a bit, but whether we get another late sell-off is another question," he said.
Howard said the minutes from the July FOMC and the Philadelphia Fed survey, both due on Thursday, would likely be the most interesting events of the week for Treasuries.
"The July FOMC minutes will be watched for whether the Fed retained its tightening bias," he said.
By 0946 GMT, September T-bonds were up 10/32 at 113-30.
